item.title: Researchers warn against sole dependence on HbA1c to diagnose, monitor diabetes in India
item.description: New Delhi, Feb 10: Researchers are cautioning against relying solely on glycated haemoglobin, ‘HbA1c’, for diagnosing and monitoring diabetes in South Asia, especially India, as the high prevalence of anaemia and blood disorders can complicate the interpretation of values. item.title: Study suggests people with obesity 70 pc more likely to be hospitalised, die from infectious disease
item.description: NEW DELHI, Feb 10: People with obesity could be 70 per cent more likely to be hospitalised or die from an infectious disease, including flu, COVID-19 and pneumonia, according to a study published in The Lancet journal. In 2023, obesity was linked to one in ten infection-related global deaths, researchers said, even as they said estimates of obesity’s global impact should be interpreted with caution. item.title: 58 genetic variants, not single gene, shape anxiety risk: Study
item.description: New Delhi, Feb 11: Researchers have found 58 genetic variants linked to an increased risk of anxiety, suggesting that the disorder is not driven by a “single anxiety gene”. The researchers, led by those from Texas A&M University in the US, said that anxiety disorders are influenced by genetic variants from across the human genome, with each variant inherited subtly changing an individual’s genetic risk for developing anxiety-related conditions.
